transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

...Just having some issues at my apartment. The people there are watching my comings and goings. They keep slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, but... I know what it is. So, that's why I came in.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No. ...I don't hear things like that. Just... no.
Have you been feeling unusually high or energized lately?
No. I don't... I haven't been feeling like that. Just... normal, I guess. Not high or energized.
How long have you been feeling that people at your apartment are watching you and sending notes about you?
...About a year. Maybe a year and a month. Something like that.
During this past year, have you had a period of at least a couple of weeks when you felt very depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

...Yeah. I guess so. Most mornings... I wake up and there's just this... heavy feeling. Like it's hollow. It's like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. So... yeah, mostly every day.
Have there been times when you felt watched or targeted even when you were not feeling depressed?

...Yeah. There was a... a spell of a few weeks, maybe. I was eating a bit better. Wasn't waking up quite so... hopeless, I guess. But... they were still watching my door. The neighbors. Reporting on me. That didn't change.
Have you ever had a time when the feeling that people were watching or reporting on you went away completely?
...No. Not really. It's... it's always there. Even if I don't see them looking, I know they are. It never really stops.
Over the past year, have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?
...I don't know. I guess I don't talk much anyway. There's just... not much to say.
Have you ever had a seizure?
...No. I haven't. Never had one of those.
Have you found that you care much less about things than you used to?

...Yeah. I suppose. I used to do things. Choir practice... playing bridge. I'd cook beans on Sundays, do little repair jobs for folks around here. But... I don't know. Now I mostly just let the phone ring. Just... tell myself there's no point going.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

...I guess sometimes. People give me this look. Like... like I skipped half the story. I'll try to explain something, you know... I'll start talking about the rent, and then... the marina, and the choir robes... and the wires in the walls. And they just stare at me. So I just... don't say much anymore.
Have people told you that your face seems less expressive or that your voice sounds flat?
...No. I don't think so. Nobody's said anything like that to me. But... like I said, I don't really see people enough for them to notice anyway.
Have you had problems with your memory?
...No. Not really. I remember things okay, I guess.
Do you believe there are wires in the walls that are being used to monitor or control you?
...I don't know what you mean. I just... I know there are wires. That's just how buildings are made. I never said anything about... being monitored.
Do you believe anyone can control your thoughts?
...No. Nobody controls what I think. That doesn't... that doesn't really make sense. They're just my thoughts.
Have there been times when it felt hard to start or keep doing everyday activities, even simple things?
...No. I do what needs doing. It's... just regular stuff. I get by alright, I guess.
Before all this started, were you generally able to manage your work, home responsibilities, and relationships normally?

...I guess things used to be easier. Lately... I don't know. I've missed some appointments. The bills pile up sometimes. I just... I haven't been going to church or doing my volunteer stuff. It's just hard to keep track of the days, and... I just don't really want to deal with people right now.
Do you believe the people at your apartment can do things to you that would be impossible in ordinary life?
...No. I don't know what you mean by that. They're just... neighbors. They don't do anything to me. I just stay in my apartment.
During the past year, has that depressed mood been present for most of the time?
...Yeah, I guess. Since I moved, mostly. Even when my head isn't as... mixed up, I still just feel down. Like I'm no use to anybody. Just don't care about much anymore.
During that depressed time, did you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

...I suppose. I used to like doing things. Choir practice... playing bridge. I'd cook up a pot of beans on Sundays, maybe help folks out with little repair jobs around their places. But... lately, I just... I hear the phone ring and I just let it go. Tell myself there ain't no point in going anywhere anyway.

patient.answer: ...Just having some issues at my apartment. The people there are watching my comings and goings. They keep slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, but... I know what it is. So, that's why I came in.

inference.note: Initial candidate set based on persecutory delusional content. Added primary psychotic disorders, mood disorders with psychotic features, brief/acute psychosis, and psychosis due to a medical condition; no clear evidence yet to narrow further.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the suspicious belief is accompanied by auditory hallucinations, which would help distinguish psychotic disorders from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hallucinations (hearing voices), which is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No. ...I don't hear things like that. Just... no.

inference.note: No auditory hallucinations reported, but this alone does not sufficiently narrow the differential yet.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory belief is mood-congruent psychosis occurring during a manic episode, helping distinguish bipolar disorder with psychotic symptoms from primary psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling unusually high or energized lately?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of mania (feeling unusually high or energized), which is not part of my symptom profile (Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type).

patient.answer: No. I don't... I haven't been feeling like that. Just... normal, I guess. Not high or energized.

inference.note: Denied auditory hallucinations and denied elevated/energized mood, which lowers suspicion for hallucination-driven psychosis and mania, but does not yet rule out the prior differential.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief has lasted long enough to distinguish a persistent psychotic disorder from an acute/transient episode.
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling that people at your apartment are watching you and sending notes about you?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The suspicious thoughts about the apartment neighbors and office have been with me for about a year and a month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the patient has been experiencing the delusions about people watching him and sending notes to the office, which corresponds to the duration of the psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer: ...About a year. Maybe a year and a month. Something like that.

inference.note: Duration >1 year with persistent persecutory delusions supports a chronic psychotic disorder and argues against acute/transient psychotic disorder (F23.3). Denial of elevated mood makes bipolar psychosis (F31.2) less likely, and absence of depressive features makes severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3) less likely.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a mood syndrome occurring alongside the psychosis to distinguish schizophrenia/delusional disorder from schizoaffective disorder.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have ever occurred outside of a mood episode, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from a mood disorder with psychotic features and helps separate it from delusional disorder/schizophrenia-spectrum conditions.
doctor.question: Have there been times when you felt watched or targeted even when you were not feeling depressed?

patient.answer: ...Yeah. There was a... a spell of a few weeks, maybe. I was eating a bit better. Wasn't waking up quite so... hopeless, I guess. But... they were still watching my door. The neighbors. Reporting on me. That didn't change.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the delusions ever went away completely, which is not explicitly covered in the symptom profile. patient.answer: ...No. Not really. It's... it's always there. Even if I don't see them looking, I know they are. It never really stops.

doctor.question: During the past year, has that depressed mood been present for most of the time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent persecutory delusions have been present for about a year, including during a period of a few weeks when mood symptoms improved, establishing psychosis outside a mood episode. The patient also reports depressed mood present for most of the year with clear anhedonia and reduced engagement, indicating a substantial mood episode concurrent with psychotic illness. Schizophrenia was considered due to disorganized/derailment-like speech and negative symptoms, but the prominent, sustained depressive syndrome favors schizoaffective disorder. Delusional disorder was considered because the delusions are mainly persecutory and non-bizarre, but mood symptoms and thought-disorganization-like features make it less fitting.
